newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Sept 18.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Sept. 18:

WASHINGTON - The Commission on Presidential Debates unanimously recommended that Reform Party candidate Ross Perot be excluded from this year's presidential debates, arguing that he had no "realistic chance" to win the presidency.

WASHINGTON - President Clinton announced the deployment of 3,500 additional troops to Kuwait and the administration said it sent Iraqi President Saddam Hussein a new set of demands he must meet or face military action.
WASHINGTON - A federal jury convicted a local man of involuntary manslaughter for his part in an April 17 car crash that killed three people.
WASHINGTON - Republicans gave ground on education spending and struggled for a way out of their impasse over immigration.
WASHINGTON - Employee drug testing has become the norm among U.S. corporations.

WASHINGTON - Federal Reserve officials were astonished by the apparent leak of one of their most closely held monetary policy secrets, a recommendation by eight of the 12 regional Fed governors to raise a key interest rate.
BLOOMINGTON, MINNESOTA - The Mall of America will institute a curfew banning all unescorted youths under 16 from the mall on weekends.
